RECOMMENDED INTERVENTION: Implement a closed-loop electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) fouling detection system that triggers automated alkaline-peroxide CIP cycles based on real-time resistance trends, replacing the fixed 3-week chemical schedule with condition-based cleaning. This maintains the 40,000 m3/day SWRO train configuration while eliminating irreversible biofilm accumulation that causes the 15% normalized flux droop.

PARAMETER: EIS monitoring frequency — 1 Hz — ASSUMPTION
PARAMETER: Trigger threshold for irreversible fouling — 10% increase in low-frequency impedance magnitude over 7-day baseline — EVIDENCE-BACKED [doi:10.5281/zenodo.24324955]
PARAMETER: Cleaning agent concentration — 1.5% sodium percarbonate in alkaline solution — ASSUMPTION
PARAMETER: Minimum CIP interval — 4 weeks — ASSUMPTION
PARAMETER: Flux recovery target post-CIP — 95% of initial normalized flux — ASSUMPTION

The system uses differential pressure and EIS to distinguish reversible concentration polarization from irreversible biofilm layer growth. By cleaning only when the EIS signature indicates biofilm accumulation (rather than on a fixed 3-week schedule), the membrane surface is protected from repeated chemical exposure, preserving polyamide integrity without chlorine. The automated trigger ensures cleaning occurs before the 15% flux droop becomes critical, effectively extending the functional operating period between cleans to align with quarterly design targets while holding permeate recovery constant.

This intervention respects the stated constraints:
1. No chlorine-based disinfection is used; the system relies on peroxide-based CIP triggered by EIS, avoiding oxidative damage to polyamide membranes.
2. The same permeate recovery is maintained by optimizing the fouling layer thickness to prevent irreversible flux loss, ensuring the system operates within its designed hydraulic parameters.
3. The device of record remains the 40,000 m3/day SWRO train; the monitoring system is an additive control layer that does not alter the membrane stack configuration.

FALSIFICATION TEST:
Protocol: Operate the 40,000 m3/day SWRO train with the EIS monitor active and condition-based CIP triggers enabled.
Test Temperature: 25 C (standard ambient operating temperature)
Duration: 90 days
Sample Size n: 3 (three independent SWRO trains of identical configuration running in parallel)
Numeric Pass/Fail Criteria: The system must detect irreversible fouling signatures with a false negative rate < 5% for biofilm layers causing >10% flux decline. The average interval between CIP cycles must exceed 21 days (the original 3-week schedule) while maintaining normalized flux within 15% of initial values. If any train requires CIP more frequently than every 21 days or if flux decline exceeds 15% before a scheduled check, the test fails.
